The '''2013–14 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] during the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team's [[head coach]] was [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]], who is in his 11th season as UNC's head men's basketball coach. They played their home games at the [[Dean E. Smith Center]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the season 24–10, 13–5 in ACC play to finish in a tie for third place. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2014 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] to Pittsburgh. They received an at-large bid to the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated Providence in the second round before losing in the third round to Iowa State.

==Pre-season==
The Tar Heels entered the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]] lost two starters from the previous season as [[Dexter Strickland]] graduated and second team All-ACC shooting guard [[Reggie Bullock]] declared for the [[2013 NBA draft]].  However, rising juniors and potential draft picks [[James Michael McAdoo]] and [[P. J. Hairston]] decided to return to Chapel Hill and UNC brought in a strong recruiting class including [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-Americans]] Kennedy Meeks and Isaiah Hicks.

Another offseason change involved the coaching staff as long-time Roy Williams assistant Joe Holladay retired.  UNC alum Brad Frederick joined the staff as Director of Basketball Operations in June.  Frederick came from the coaching staff at [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], where he had been for 14 seasons.  He is the son of former Kansas Athletic Director Bob Frederick.<ref>{{cite web | last = Carter | first = Andrew | title = Brad Frederick named UNC director of basketball operations | work = [[Raleigh News and Observer]] | date = June 3, 2013 | url = http://blogs.newsobserver.com/uncnow/brad-frederick-named-unc-director-of-basketball-operations | access-date = January 4, 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140106032329/http://blogs.newsobserver.com/uncnow/brad-frederick-named-unc-director-of-basketball-operations | archive-date = 2014-01-06 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

However, the optimism of the Spring turned to uncertainty in the Summer as both Hairston and fifth year senior [[Leslie McDonald]] were both suspended from the team due to eligibility concerns, leaving only two scholarship guards (sophomore [[Marcus Paige]] and freshman Nate Britt) on the roster entering the season.  McDonald would be reinstated in the non-conference season, but Hairston's suspension would hold for the entire season.<ref name=USAT>{{cite web | last = Auerbach | first = Nicole | title = NCAA clears UNC's Leslie McDonald but P.J. Hairston could sit season | work = [[USA Today]] | date = December 18, 2013| url = https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/12/18/ncaa-clears-uncs-leslie-mcdonald-but-pj-hairston-could-sit-season/4113317/ | access-date = January 4, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last = Brown | first = C. L. | title = Tar Heels won't seek reinstatement | work = [[ESPN.com]] | date = December 20, 2013| url = https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10172154/north-carolina-tar-heels-not-applying-ncaa-reinstatement-pj-hairston?ex_cid=espnapi_public | access-date = January 4, 2014}}</ref>

Even with this uncertainty, North Carolina was voted #13 in the AP preseason poll<ref>{{cite web | last = Norlander | first = Matt | title = AP preseason poll released: UK at top; MSU, 'Ville, Duke, KU follow | work = [[CBSSports.com]] | date = October 31, 2013| url = http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24166158/ap-preseason-poll-released-uk-at-top-msu-ville-duke-ku-follow | access-date = January 4, 2014}}</ref> and #11 in the USA Today Coaches' Poll.<ref>{{cite web | last = Auerbach | first = Nicole | title = Analysis: A look at every top 25 team in the college hoops coaches poll | work = [[USA Today]] | date = October 18, 2013| url = https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/10/17/analysis-top-25-teams-college-basketball-coaches-poll-top-25-rankings/2998175/ | access-date = January 4, 2014}}</ref>  The ACC media tabbed the Tar Heels third in the conference preseason poll.<ref>{{cite web | title = Media Picks Tar Heels Third In ACC | work = [[North Carolina Tar Heels]] | date = October 16, 2013| url = http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209285247 | access-date = January 4, 2014}}</ref>

The top-rated recruit in the class scheduled to start college in Fall 2013 is Isaiah Hicks, the eighth ranked power forward and the 18th ranked player in the ESPN 100.<ref name="ESPN">{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/order/true|title = ESPN Basketball Recruiting - Player Rankings}}</ref> Shortly behind him in that ranking is Kennedy Meeks at #59. He is the #6 ranked center in the 2013 high school class. Britt is the 52nd ranked player in the current high school class and 11th point guard. He tore his meniscus in December 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.fayobserver.com/accbasketball/December-2012/Nate-Britt,-a-North-Carolina-signee,-is-currently- |title = Blogs - Fayobserver.com - Nate Britt, a North Carolina signee, is currently sidelined with a torn meniscus  |access-date=2013-03-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130406155702/http://blogs.fayobserver.com/accbasketball/December-2012/Nate-Britt,-a-North-Carolina-signee,-is-currently- |archive-date=2013-04-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Season==

===Non-conference play===
The Tar Heels started the season with uncertainty as Hairston's and McDonald's eligibility cases remained in limbo for the first nine games of the season.  After uneventful victories over [[2013–14 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]] and [[2013–14 Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball team|Holy Cross]], the Heels were stunned 83–80 at home by [[2013–14 Belmont Bruins men's basketball team|Belmont]], in part because of a 22–48 performance at the [[free throw]] line.<ref>{{cite web | title = Belmont stuns No. 12 North Carolina with late 3-pointer | work = [[ESPN.com]] | date = November 17, 2013| url = https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400502680 | access-date = January 5, 2014}}</ref>  However, the team would redeem themselves by beating #3 [[2013–14 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] in the [[Hall of Fame Tip Off]] championship.  Marcus Paige led the team with 32 points while post players Brice Johnson and Kennedy Meeks controlled the paint and the Heels won 93–84.  Paige was named ACC Player of the Week for his performance against the Cardinals and the [[2013–14 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond Spiders]] in the previous game (26 points).<ref>{{cite web| title =UNC's Marcus Paige Named ACC Hoops Player Of The Week| work =WFMY News| date =November 25, 2013| url =http://www.digtriad.com/sports/local/article/307298/13/UNCs-Marcus-Paige-Named-ACC-Hoops-Player-Of-The-Week| access-date =January 5, 2014| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20140106041427/http://www.digtriad.com/sports/local/article/307298/13/UNCs-Marcus-Paige-Named-ACC-Hoops-Player-Of-The-Week| archive-date =2014-01-06| url-status =dead}}</ref>

North Carolina's inconsistency would show itself again as the Heels lost their next game - an 83–86 contest at [[2013–14 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]], coached by former [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] assistant [[Jerod Haase]].  But true to form, the Heels bounced back and beat #1 [[2013–14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] on the road in a game they never trailed.  Kennedy Meeks led the team in scoring with 15 and was named ACC Rookie of the Week.<ref>{{cite web| last = Friedlander| first = Brett| title = UNC's Kennedy Meeks named ACC Rookie of the Week| work = [[Wilmington Star News]]| date = December 9, 2013| url = http://acc.blogs.starnewsonline.com/39453/uncs-kennedy-meeks-named-acc-rookie-of-the-week/| access-date = January 5, 2014| archive-date = January 6, 2014| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140106040724/http://acc.blogs.starnewsonline.com/39453/uncs-kennedy-meeks-named-acc-rookie-of-the-week/| url-status = dead}}</ref>  After an easy home win over [[2013–14 UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball team|UNC Greensboro]] (coached by [[Wes Miller]], another Williams disciple), the Tar Heels completed a sweep of the top three teams in the preseason polls by upending #11 Kentucky at the [[Dean Smith Center]].  Paige and James Michael McAdoo were the stars, scoring 23 and 20 points respectively.<ref>{{cite web | title = Marcus Paige scores 21 in 2nd half as UNC upends Kentucky | work = [[ESPN.com]] | date = December 14, 2013| url = https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400502733 | access-date = January 5, 2014}}</ref>

On December 18, the team received the news that Leslie McDonald would be reinstated in time for the Texas game at the Smith Center.<ref name=USAT/>  However, the Tar Heels lost to the young Longhorns.  North Carolina finished their non-conference season with wins over [[2013–14 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]], [[2013–14 Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball team|Northern Kentucky]] and [[2013–14 UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball team|UNC Wilmington]].

===Conference play===
The Tar Heels started 1–4 in conference play, but then, they won twelve straight, including a win over #5 Duke on February 20. With the Duke win, North Carolina became the first team to defeat each of the [[AP Poll]] preseason top 4 in the same season in the 53 years that the poll has released preseason rankings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400537134|title=Unranked North Carolina rallies to topple No. 5 Duke, win 8th straight|access-date=2014-02-25|date=2014-02-20|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> The streak was broken with a loss at Duke in Cameron Indoor Stadium.
